parole.testo: From buccal, from Latin bucca (“mouth; cheek”). By surface analysis, bucc- + -o-.

parole.significato: Of or relating to the nation of Germany.
parole.testo: From Latin Germānus, Germānī (“the peoples of Germānia”), as distinct from Gauls (in the writings of Caesar and Tacitus), and of uncertain ultimate origin (possibly Celtic/Gaulish). Not related to german (“closely related”) or germane (from the Latin adjective germānus, through Old French). Attested

parole.significato: An Italic tribe of ancient Italy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin umbrī. Also called Ombrii in some Roman sources. Many Roman writers thought the Umbri to be Celtic; Cornelius Bocchus wrote that they descended from an ancient Gaulish tribe.
